[USER] User expressed interest in the outcome of Thomas More's opposition to the Church of England and its impact on future religious and political life in England.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Thomas More's opposition led to his execution for treason in 1535 due to his refusal to accept King Henry VIII as the head of the Church and recognize the annulment of Henry's marriage to Catherine of Aragon.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] More's actions solidified the separation of the Anglican Church from the Roman Catholic Church and established Henry VIII as the supreme head of the Anglican Church.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] More's martyrdom became a symbol for Catholics in England and around the world.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] More's writings, particularly "Utopia," influenced political thought in England and Europe, impacting ideas about social justice, individual rights, and the rule of law.
